related_questions.snippet: The IRS treats cryptocurrency as “property.” If you buy, sell or exchange cryptocurrency, you're likely on the hook for paying crypto taxes. Reporting your crypto activity requires using Form 1040 Schedule D as your crypto tax form to reconcile your capital gains and losses and Form 8949 if necessary.

related_questions.question: How much does IRS tax cryptocurrency?
related_questions.snippet: Short-term gains from crypto held a year or less are taxed at ordinary-income rates (10-37%). Long-term gains from crypto held more than a year are taxed at lower rates (0-20%). Income you receive in crypto (whether as payment, mining rewards, or staking yield) is taxed at ordinary-income rates when received.
